goldens.comment: Using retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1 reads a possibly stale value and can lose increments under concurrency; consider an atomic increment via Prisma (increment: 1) to avoid race conditions (also applies to the similar update in the catch block).
goldens.reasoning: G1 is about a lost-update race: retryCount + 1 reads a value that may be stale, so the fix is an atomic increment. C2 is about the update throwing when the reminder was deleted concurrently, which is a different failure.

goldens.comment: The deletion logic in scheduleSMSReminders.ts incorrectly deletes non-SMS workflow reminders (e.g., Email, WhatsApp) that have retryCount > 1. This occurs because the retryCount condition within the OR clause for deletion lacks a method: WorkflowMethods.SMS filter, causing it to apply to all reminder types instead of only SMS reminders, which is the intended scope of this function.
goldens.reasoning: C1 describes the same issue: the retryCount OR branch has no SMS method filter, so it deletes non-SMS reminders.

candidates: The second OR branch in the deleteMany query deletes ANY WorkflowReminder with retryCount > 1 regardless of method type, because it lacks a method: WorkflowMethods.SMS filter, causing non-SMS reminders (EMAIL, WHATSAPP) to be unintentionally deleted by the SMS cron job

In scheduleSMSReminders, the catch block calls prisma.workflowReminder.update() to increment retryCount, but that update can throw if the reminder was deleted concurrently, escaping the catch and aborting the entire cron run
